BURSEVI:v6p353/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p353/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p353/r1.claim: Those described as patient modify “the workers,” or are an accusative of praise; their patience covers persecution, migration's hardship, and other trials.
BURSEVI:v6p353/r1.anchor: صفة للعاملين أو نصب على المدح أي صبروا على أذية المشركين

BURSEVI:v6p353/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p353/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p353/r2.claim: They rely only on God; strong faith loosens attachment to homeland, property, and provision, makes exile and home alike, and leaves God's reward sufficient.
BURSEVI:v6p353/r2.anchor: لا يعتمدون في أمورهم إلا على الله تعالى وهذا التوكل من قوة الإيمان

BURSEVI:v6p353/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p353/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p353/r3.claim: A hadith says that someone who flees with his religion even a short distance merits Paradise and companionship with Abraham and Muhammad; he merits Paradise for giving up home for religion and their company by following their migration and reviving their practice.
BURSEVI:v6p353/r3.anchor: من فر بدينه من أرض إلى أرض ولو كان شبرا استوجب الجنة

BURSEVI:v6p353/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p353/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p353/r4.claim: For the spiritual traveler, migration means leaving the land of social prestige and public acceptance for obscurity.
BURSEVI:v6p353/r4.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن السالك ينبغي أن يهاجر من أرض الجاه

BURSEVI:v6p353/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p353/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
BURSEVI:v6p353/r5.claim: When his reputation became so great that people competed to buy a melon that fell from his hand, he left; he was content to live where people called him an unbeliever and stoned him twice a day.
BURSEVI:v6p353/r5.anchor: حكايت كنند از ابو سعيد خراز قدس سره كفت در شهرى بودم

BURSEVI:v6p353/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p353/r6.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
BURSEVI:v6p353/r6.claim: He said he had felt worldly joy only three times; in Antioch he went barefoot and bareheaded, welcomed being called a runaway slave, and told his self that if it had fled, it could now return peacefully.
BURSEVI:v6p353/r6.anchor: واز ابراهيم ادهم قدس سره حكايت كنند كه كفت

SULAMI:v2p119#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p119#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن علي
SULAMI:v2p119#2/r1.claim: When patience matures it leads to gratitude and contentment; sound patience supports trust in God, grows from certainty, and is unavailable without certainty.
SULAMI:v2p119#2/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن علي : للصبر أول فإذا تحقق في أوله واستكمل له مقامه أداه صبره إلى الشكر

SULAMI:v2p119#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p119#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p119#2/r2.claim: Patience is keeping good company with affliction just as one does with ease; anything else is merely forced endurance.
SULAMI:v2p119#2/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : الصبر المقام مع البلاء يحسن الصحبة كالمقام مع العافية

SULAMI:v2p119#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p119#2/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
SULAMI:v2p119#2/r3.claim: Patience means receiving affliction with a spacious heart.
SULAMI:v2p119#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق : الصبر تلقى البلاء الرحب والدعة

SULAMI:v2p119#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p119#2/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
SULAMI:v2p119#2/r4.claim: Trust in God is agitation without stillness and stillness without agitation.
SULAMI:v2p119#2/r4.anchor: سئل أبو سعيد الخراز عن التوكل فقال : هو اضطراب بلا سكون وسكون بلا اضطراب

SULAMI:v2p119#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p119#2/r5.speaker: الجريري
SULAMI:v2p119#2/r5.claim: Al-Jurayri approves al-Kharrāz's paradoxical definition of trust in God as a good statement.
SULAMI:v2p119#2/r5.anchor: قال الجريري : وهذا قول حسن في التوكل

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the patient are those who persevere in obeying God's command.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير الذين صبروا يعني على امر الله

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r2.speaker: عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r2.claim: Umar says patience is of two kinds.

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr describes patience as the servant's acknowledgment.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r3.anchor: وقول سعيد بن جبير الصبر اعتراف العبد

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains reliance on their Lord as hoping in no one besides Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3078/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله وعلى ربهم يتوكلون قال : لا يرجون غيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r13.claim: Patience and reliance on God gather all good, including patience in obedience and restraint from desires.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r13.anchor: ثم وصفهم تعالى بالصبر والتوكل وهاتان جماع الخير كله أي الصبر على الطاعات وعن الشهوات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r1.claim: The patient remain steadfast in faith, migrate, leave enemies and even family and kin for God's sake, and trust their Lord in religious and worldly affairs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r1.anchor: على دينهم، وهاجروا إلى الله، ونابذوا الأعداء، وفارقوا الأهل والأقرباء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r2.speaker: أبو مالك الأشعري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r2.claim: The Prophet says God prepared transparent chambers for those who feed others, speak well, fast, and pray while people sleep.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r2.anchor: أعدها الله لمن أطعم الطعام، وأطاب الكلام، وأباح الصيام، وأقام الصلاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r3.claim: Trust in God applies in every circumstance, religious or worldly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r3.anchor: في أحوالهم كلها، في دينهم ودنياهم

MUQATIL:29:56-63/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:56-63/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:56-63/r2.claim: God reminds migrants that everyone dies and returns for judgment; faithful, righteous migrants receive eternal rooms with rivers, and those patient through migration trust God despite lacking money or livelihood in Medina.
MUQATIL:29:56-63/r2.anchor: ثم خوفهم الموت ليهاجروا، فقال تعالى: { كل نفس ذآئقة الموت ثم إلينا ترجعون } [آية: 57]

NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#6/r1.claim: الذين صبروا may predicate an omitted subject, listing patience in leaving home, facing polytheists, trials, calamities, obedience, and avoiding sins.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#6/r1.anchor: خبر مبتدأ محذوف أى هم الذين صبروا على مفارقة الأوطان وعلى أذى المشركين وعلى المحن والمصائب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#6/r2.claim: Connecting الذين to the previous verse as a modifier of العاملين is better than starting a new clause.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#6/r2.anchor: والوَصل أجود ليكون الذين نعتا للعاملين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#6/r3.claim: They rely on God alone through all these hardships.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#6/r3.anchor: ﴿ وعلى ربهم يتوكلون ﴾ ولم يتوكلوا فى جميع ذلك إلا على الله

SAMIN-DURR:29:59/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:59/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:59/r1.claim: الذين صبروا allows genitive, accusative, or nominative, as in analogous constructions discussed earlier.
SAMIN-DURR:29:59/r1.anchor: يجوز فيه الجر والنصب والرفع كنظائر له تقدمت

RAZI-FULL:v25p76#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p76#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p76#2/r1.claim: Patience suits present hardship, while reliance suits future needs; the past cannot be recovered or altered.
RAZI-FULL:v25p76#2/r1.anchor: ذكر أمرين الصبر والتوكل لأن الزمان ماض وحاضر ومستقبل لكن الماضي لا تدارك له

RAZI-FULL:v25p76#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p76#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p76#2/r2.claim: Patience and reliance require knowledge of God and of the passing world: knowing worldly things are transient makes patience easier, while knowing God endures supports trust in His provision.
RAZI-FULL:v25p76#2/r2.anchor: فمن علم ما سواه علم أنه زائل فيهون عليه الصبر إذ الصبر على الزائل هين

RAZI-FULL:v25p76#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p76#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p76#2/r3.claim: The surrounding exhortation suits two groups: those able to leave a place of harm rely on God and migrate, while those unable to leave endure harm and continue worshipping.
RAZI-FULL:v25p76#2/r3.anchor: فحصل الناس على قسمين قادر على الخروج وهو متوكل على ربه ، يترك الأوطان ويفارق الأخوان

STUDYQURAN:29:58/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:58/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:58/r4.claim: Unlike disbelievers who demand the punishment be hastened, believers patiently endure the present and trust God for what He will provide in the future.
STUDYQURAN:29:58/r4.anchor: such individuals are patient with what confronts them in the present and trust in their Lord regarding what He will provide them

TABATABAI:29:59-60/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:59-60/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:59-60/r1.claim: God first promises reward to believers with good works, calls them workers, then defines those workers as patient and reliant on their Lord; patience and reliance characterize true believers.
TABATABAI:29:59-60/r1.anchor: وقد بين تعالى أولا ثواب الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ثم سماهم عاملين إذ قال { ونعم أجر العاملين } ثم فسر العاملين

TABATABAI:29:59-60/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:59-60/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:59-60/r2.claim: Believers should endure harm while religious life remains possible; if they cannot practice their religion in their land, they should migrate and endure the hardship that follows.
TABATABAI:29:59-60/r2.anchor: فعلى المؤمن أن يصبر في الله على كل أذى وجفوة ما يجد إلى العيشة الدينية سبيلا

TABATABAI:29:59-60/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:59-60/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:59-60/r3.claim: Patience includes endurance in calamity, obedience, and resisting sin, though the Meccan context particularly means patience under persecution.
TABATABAI:29:59-60/r3.anchor: والصبر أعم من الصبر عند المصيبة والصبر على الطاعة والصبر على المعصية

TABRISI:29:58-60/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:58-60/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:58-60/r8.claim: Alladhīna ṣabarū may be a genitive adjective for al-ʿāmilīn, with the praised subject omitted; alternatively, an implied iḍāfa makes the patient ones' reward the omitted subject.
TABRISI:29:58-60/r8.anchor: في موضع جر صفة للعالمين ويكون المخصوص بالمدح محذوفا

TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r8.claim: They endured hardship and harm without abandoning their religion, patiently performed demanding acts of worship, and relied on God in important affairs and migration.
TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r8.anchor: على دينهم فلم يتركوه لشدة نالتهم وأذى لحقهم

THALABI:v7p288/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p288/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p288/r4.claim: The believers praised here are those who patiently endure and rely on their Lord.
THALABI:v7p288/r4.anchor: خالدين فيها نعم أجر العاملين الذين صبروا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p553/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p553/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p553/r1.claim: The migrants endured their religion, hunger, distress, and the loss of their property, children, and homes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p553/r1.anchor: ابن عباس: على دينهم، وعلى المخمصة، وعلى الجزع، وترك الأموال والأولاد والدور

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p553/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p553/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p553/r2.claim: To rely on God means to trust Him in the migration; Ibn ʿAbbās applies this to migrants who left their houses and property.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p553/r2.anchor: وبالله يثقون في هجرتهم (¬4). قال ابن عباس: ذلك أن المهاجرين توكلوا على الله وتركوا دورهم وأموالهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p553/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p553/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p553/r3.claim: Muqātil says migrants in Mecca worried they had no home or livelihood in Medina, so God admonished them to take heed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p553/r3.anchor: مقاتل: إن أحدهم كان يقول بمكة: كيف أهاجر إلى المدينة وليس لي بها دار ولا معيشة؟ فوعظهم الله ليعتبروا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p638#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p638#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p638#2/r3.claim: The praised believers are those who are patient and rely on their Lord.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r9.claim: The patient endure leaving their homelands, migration, and every hardship in obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions; patience and reliance on God comprise all good.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r9.anchor: الذين صبروا: أي على مفارقة أوطانهم والهجرة وجميع المشاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r10.claim: When Muslims in Mecca were ordered to migrate, they feared poverty as strangers without homes, property, or anyone to feed them; the animals' example reassures them that God provides even for creatures unable to stock provisions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r10.anchor: ولما أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، من أسلم بمكة بالهجرة، خافوا الفقر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p11/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p11/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p11/r1.claim: Alladhina ṣabarū may modify the workers, be the predicate of an omitted subject, or be an accusative of praise.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p11/r1.anchor: صفة للعاملين أو خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو نصب على المدح

ALUSI-FULL:v21p11/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p11/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p11/r2.claim: Their patience is through unbelievers' abuse, the hardships of migration, and other trials; they rely on God alone in all they do and leave undone.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p11/r2.anchor: صبروا على أذية المشركين وشدائد المهاجرة وغير ذلك من المحن والمشاق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252#2/r1.claim: The patient endured hardships without abandoning their religion when distress struck; they rely on their Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252#2/r1.anchor: {الذين صبروا} على الشدائد ولم يتركوا دينهم لشدة لحقتهم، {وعلى ربهم يتوكلون} يعتمدون.

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r4.claim: The patient endure pagan abuse, migration for religion, and other trials; they rely on their Lord alone.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r4.anchor: على أذية المشركين والهجرة للدين إلى غير ذلك من المحن والمشاق. { وعلى ربهم يتوكلون } ولا يتوكلون إلا على الله.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r10.claim: They rely only on their Lord, renewing their trust in him in every matter, including provision after migration and struggle against enemies, rather than depending on family or homeland.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r10.anchor: أي وحده لا على أهل ولا وطن
